ru: На ночь хозя́ин за́пер бы все две́ри.
en: The owner would have locked all the doors for the night.
note: Perfective бы+past is a single completed hypothetical event, so "would have locked"; «на ночь» is "for the night" (as in this word's own imperative example), not habitual "at night".

en_alt: Lock the gates for the night.
note: «воро́та» is plural-only and is rendered "the gates" in this word's other example, so accept both.
Frame-only collision, but an imperative against the partner's "I write down important thoughts" leaves an obvious cue.

ru: На моём ме́сте вы записа́ли бы а́дрес.
en_alt: In my place, you would have written down the address.
note: Perfective бы+past also carries the past-counterfactual reading, which the current English does not offer.

ru: Я запи́сываю ва́жные мы́сли в блокно́т.
note: Habitual present is the right imperfective reading; the partner is an imperative, so the frame match is not confusable.

ru: Я чуть не запла́кал от ра́дости.

en: From the hurt I would have burst into tears.
note: "From hurt" is not idiomatic English, and the perfective бы+past reads as a single completed event.

ru: Она́ заплати́ла бы нали́чными, но забы́ла кошелёк.
note: Perfective already reads as a completed counterfactual event.
The idiomatic Russian for bills is «Все счета́ опла́чены»; «запла́чены» with счета́ as subject is marginal, so a native check is worth making before the English is judged.
Perfective future is correctly a bare "will pay"; the frame match is with a платить sentence whose own English is the weak half.

en_alt: Soon the authorities will ban the sale.
note: "ban the sale" is the more usual English collocation and should not be marked wrong.

ru: Хоро́ший учи́тель не запрети́л бы ученика́м задава́ть вопро́сы.

note: Perfective future is correctly "will forbid"; the frame collision sits on the запрещать side.
The impersonal 3rd-plural is standardly rendered by an English passive; the literal "They forbid smoking here" would be worse English.

ru: Но́вые пра́вила бу́дут запреща́ть шум по́сле оди́ннадцати.
note: Four frame collisions, but every partner is about a trip/sale/person, so the lexical cue is strong; "will be forbidding noise" is not natural English, so forcing the progressive would trade a soluble drill for a bad sentence.

ru: В большо́м го́роде она́ зараба́тывала бы бо́льше.
note: Imperfective бы is the present counterfactual "would earn"; the collision is fixed on the заработать side.

ru: На но́вой рабо́те я бу́ду зараба́тывать бо́льше.
Он зараба́тывал ма́ло, но был сча́стлив.
en: He used to earn little, but was happy.
note: Imperfective past here is habitual, and the bare "earned" collides with the perfective partner's single completed "She earned her first money".

ru: Они́ зарабо́тают мно́го на э́том де́ле.
Я зарабо́таю на маши́ну за год.

note: Single completed event; the colliding "earned" belongs to the imperfective partner, fixed there.

ru: За ле́то они́ зарабо́тали бы на пое́здку.
en: Over the summer, they would have earned enough for the trip.
note: Perfective бы+past over a bounded period is a completed event, and "would earn" duplicates the imperfective partner's present counterfactual.

ru: Ско́ро она́ зарабо́тает на свою́ мечту́.

note: Four of this word's six sentences render заслужи́ть as "earn", which the gloss "to deserve" does not cover — the headword gloss probably wants "to earn, to deserve".

ru: Че́стным трудо́м она́ заслужи́ла бы уваже́ние.
en_alt: Through honest work she would have earned respect.
note: The perfective also supports the completed past-counterfactual reading.
"deserve" is stative and sits badly in the present perfect; "you have earned it" is what an English speaker says for заслужи́ла.
"Will you deserve the reward?" is not something an English speaker would say; the perfective future here is "earn".

en: Everyone burst out laughing at the same time.
note: «одновреме́нно» is "simultaneously"; "at once" reads as "immediately" in English.

ru: От тако́й шу́тки я бы засмея́лся.
note: A general hypothetical, so the present "would burst out laughing" is right.

ru: Без шу́ма я бы засну́ла бы́стро.
en: Without noise I would have fallen asleep quickly.
note: Perfective бы+past is one completed event; the partner sentence «Без телефо́на де́ти засыпа́ли бы ра́ньше» has the same "Without X … would fall asleep …" shape, so the drill currently has two right answers.

ru: На ва́шем ме́сте я не заставля́ла бы его́ ждать.
en_alt: In your place I would not make him wait.
note: "If I were you" is a fine idiom, but the literal "In your place" tracks «На ва́шем ме́сте» and should be accepted.

ru: Тре́нер бу́дет заставля́ть нас бе́гать ка́ждое у́тро.

en_alt: They used to make the children work.
note: The imperfective past also carries the habitual reading.

ru: Ребёнок ещё не уме́ет застёгивать пу́говицы.
en: The child does not yet know how to do up buttons.
note: «уме́ет» is "knows how to", a learned skill; "cannot" drops that and the sentence is one of the few showing уме́ть.

ru: Он всегда́ застёгивает ку́ртку до ве́рха.

note: The imperfective present covers both the habitual and the ongoing reading.

ru: Она́ бы застегну́ла замо́к, е́сли бы успе́ла.
note: The English is right, but the tap-hint for «замо́к» shows "lock" while the sentence needs "zip/clasp" — the gloss, not the sentence, is the half to look at.

ru: Я застегну́ пальто́ и вы́йду за́втра.
Он застегну́л все пу́говицы на пальто́.
Без огня́ суп засты́л бы на хо́лоде.
en_alt: Without a flame the soup would have set in the cold.
note: The perfective also supports the completed reading; both are natural here.

ru: Он засты́л на ме́сте от стра́ха.
Ребёнок засыпа́л на рука́х у ма́мы.
Без телефо́на де́ти засыпа́ли бы ра́ньше.
note: Habitual "would fall asleep" is exactly what the imperfective says; the perfective partner is the side corrected.

en_alt: We fall asleep late in the summer.
note: Both article choices are equally natural for «ле́том».

ru: По́сле прогу́лки я бу́ду засыпа́ть бы́стро.

note: Three of this word's sentences use the "take/grab along" sense, which the gloss "to seize" does not cover; the gloss likely needs "to seize, to take along".

ru: Я захвачу́ зонт на вся́кий слу́чай.
en_alt: I will take an umbrella just in case.
note: "take" is the plainer rendering of захвати́ть in this sense and should be accepted alongside "grab".

ru: Она́ захвати́ла бы зонт, е́сли бы зна́ла о дожде́.
Е́сли бы вы жи́ли ря́дом, то заходи́ли бы к нам ча́ще?
en: If you lived nearby, would you drop in on us more often?
note: «к нам» is dropped entirely by the current English.

ru: Отны́не я бу́ду заходи́ть к тебе́ ка́ждый ве́чер.

note: «к нам в го́сти» is the standard invitation formula; accept the idiomatic rendering too.

ru: Они́ заходи́ли к нам по вечера́м.

note: The English is right, but "to set" (of the sun) is a sense the headword gloss "to drop in" does not cover.

ru: Я ча́сто захожу́ в э́то кафе́.
Он вдруг захоте́л пое́хать к мо́рю.
Е́сли бы я уста́л, я бы захоте́л отдохну́ть.

note: Frame-only match with "You will always want more"; the content cue is unambiguous.

ru: В жару́ мне бы захоте́лось холо́дной воды́.

note: "Soon" against the partner's "Every evening" keeps the frame match answerable.

ru: При необходи́мости она́ защища́ла бы тебя́.

en_alt: The dog was defending the house.
note: "guarding" is natural but drifts from the headword gloss; the literal reading should also be accepted.

ru: Я заявлю́ об э́том в поли́цию.
note: «заяви́ть в поли́цию» is fixed as "report to the police"; a literal "declare" would not be English.

ru: Мы бы заяви́ли об э́том ра́ньше.
en_alt: We would have announced this sooner.
note: "declare this" is stiff; "announce" is the usual English for заяви́ть о чём-то and should be accepted.
«заяви́ть о свои́х права́х» is "to assert one's rights"; "declared his rights" is an odd collocation, so accept the idiomatic form too.
Same collocation point as the third-person sentence for this word.

ru: Кого́ вы бу́дете звать на пра́здник?
note: «звать на пра́здник» is "invite"; the literal "call" would mislead.

«звать на у́жин» is "invite" — as this word's own «Вы зовёте госте́й на у́жин?» already renders it — and it clears the frame collision with the perfective «Позови́ бра́та к телефо́ну» ("Call your brother to the phone").
